subject: Renewal sizing: Opportunity to optimize reserved GPUs vs. burst
messages:
From: Jordan Klein <jk@brightpath.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ameera Qureshi <ameera.q@brightpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — sizing question ahead of May 22 review

Hi Mateo / Ben,

Hope you're both well. Our renewal window with Redwood opens in three weeks and procurement asked that we come prepared with a proposal for next 12 months of dedicated capacity. High level: our Q1 usage spiked around the new summarization feature (attached). We used a mix of reserved GPUs and burst credits; procurement wants to know whether moving more of that steady traffic into reserved capacity reduces unit cost enough to justify increasing our committed tranche.

Quick context:
- Peak concurrent slices: ~42 (avg sustained window during inference-heavy hours)
- Tail latency SLOs are strict for the new product (p95 < 300ms)
- Current reserved pool: 120 H100-equivalent slots + 40 burst

Can Redwood help us with a recommended sizing delta and a conservative cost delta (annual)? We'd like a simple recommendation — keep current reserved, add N slots, or convert X% of burst to reserved — plus a rollback/fallback option if usage varies.

Attached: usage_report_q1_2028.csv (sampled per hour), short screenshots of observed latency.

Thanks — can we get a one-pager by Monday next week?

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Klein
Head of Infrastructure
BrightPath Analytics

Attachments: usage_report_q1_2028.csv (CSV, 2.3MB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — sizing question ahead of May 22 review

Jordan — thanks for the note and the dataset. I pulled the raw hourly curves and did a quick pass (see attached matrix). High level takeaways:

- There is a clear steady-state between 10:00–18:00 PT where sustained concurrent slices sit ~35–45 for several weeks.
- Burst credit consumption is concentrated in three weekday spikes. Outside of those spikes, burst sits largely unused.
- Converting 20% of burst into reserved capacity would cover ~90% of sustained daytime load and reduce per-token cost by ~8–12% in our model.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal sizing recommendation and pricing delta (Ben) — produce a 2-line commercial option: +24 reserved slots vs. conservative +12 slots (lower CAPEX commitment)
2) Operational guardrails: autoscale thresholds, canary routing to avoid p95 regressions, and a fallback to burst for 72 hours if utilization deviates >25% vs. forecast (Neha)
3) One-pager for procurement with numbers and rollback policy by EOD Monday

I've attached the preliminary capacity matrix (proposed_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx) with two scenarios and the modeled cost delta. Ben — can you write the 2-line commercial and confirm if there's room on pricing for a multi-quarter prepayment?

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Solutions — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — sizing question ahead of May 22 review

Thanks Mateo — read the matrix. Short commercial options to drop into a procurement one-pager:

Option A — Conservative cushion (recommended for risk-averse procurement)
- +12 reserved H100-equivalent slots (net reserved = 132)
- Estimated annual delta: +$342,000 (after standard volume discounts)
- Expected cost/unit reduction vs current blended: ~6%
- Benefit: Maintains 15% burst buffer for seasonal spikes

Option B — Cost-optimized (assuming commit and prepay)
- +24 reserved slots (net reserved = 144)
- Estimated annual delta: +$588,000 (with 3-month prepay applied)
- Expected cost/unit reduction vs current blended: ~11%
- Benefit: Covers 95% of sustained daytime traffic and reduces burst reliance

Operational recommendations (Neha to confirm):
- Canary 10% of traffic to reserved-only pool for 72 hours post-rollout
- Maintain prefix/KV caching for the summarization endpoint to keep p95 under 300ms
- Establish utilization alert: if reserved utilization drops below 40% for a 14-day window, trigger a review (and potential downscale conversation)

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. BrightPath prefers Option B if we can get the 3-month prepay pricing; procurement will like the larger delta in unit cost but they'll ask for a short runway to validate utilization after launch.

Let's lock Option B in principle. Two asks before we pencil it into the renewal: 
1) A short canary checklist (Ben/Neha) we can hand to our SREs — can we get that by Friday?
2) A single-slide summary with the delta numbers and rollback criteria for our procurement packet (Mateo/Ben) — aim for Friday close of business.

I can join a 30-min run-through on Thursday if you want to walk the checklist.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jordan
